summary: Reddit, X and Bluesky were blocked today, so every source is Hacker News. The strongest themes: people want meeting-notes apps that stay on the phone and aren't limited to Macs, they're fed up with devices that die when a vendor's cloud goes away, and they feel locked in or overcharged by airlines and domain registrars.

ideas.title: Private Meeting Notes for Android (Hindi/English)
ideas.oneLiner: An on-device recorder that transcribes and summarises in-person meetings and calls on a phone, with no cloud upload.
ideas.problem: Granola-style note apps are Mac-first and send audio or text to the cloud. People want something private that works on a phone and not only on Apple Silicon. Two-party-consent users hesitate to use cloud transcription at all.
ideas.targetUsers: Freelancers, consultants, founders and managers in India who hold client calls or in-person meetings on a phone and care about confidentiality.
ideas.monetization: Free tier with a monthly cap on transcription minutes. Pro at about ₹199/month, or a one-time ₹1,499. Optional cloud summaries as an add-on.
mvp: One-tap recording with a consent notice you can read aloud
On-device Whisper-class transcription, with Hindi and English
Local summary and action items using a small on-device model
Speaker labels (basic diarisation)
Searchable notes list and export to Markdown/PDF
Airplane-mode-safe: no network calls by default

competitors.name: Granola
competitors.gap: Mac-first, and audio is captured locally but notes are enhanced by cloud models.

competitors.name: Viska
competitors.gap: Offline and on both iOS and Android, but Android transcription is reported to be noticeably slower, and it doesn't focus on Indian languages.

competitors.name: Yogurt (open source)
competitors.gap: Desktop app; no phone version, which commenters pointed out.

ideas.title: Works-Offline Checker for Smart Devices
ideas.oneLiner: A product-page overlay that tells you whether a smart device or appliance keeps working without the vendor's cloud or app.
ideas.problem: Internet radios, appliances and smart devices stop working when the vendor's server goes away, and buyers can't tell this before purchase. Commenters say most appliances don't need a cloud at all, but there is no simple way to filter for the ones that don't.
ideas.targetUsers: Smart-home buyers, Home Assistant hobbyists and anyone buying a connected appliance who wants it to survive the vendor.
ideas.monetization: Free for browsing. Affiliate links to local-first alternatives. Paid API for retailers and reviewers.
mvp: Chrome/Firefox extension that matches the current product page to a device entry
Rating: fully local, local with cloud setup, cloud-required
Plain-language 'what breaks if the company shuts down' note
Community submissions with proof (a test with the internet unplugged)
Links to the matching Home Assistant or Zigbee/Matter integration
Alternatives list for each category

competitors.name: Home Assistant integration docs (IoT class)
competitors.gap: Accurate but written for people already running Home Assistant. Nothing a shopper sees on a product page.

competitors.name: Zigbee2MQTT supported devices
competitors.gap: Only covers Zigbee, and it isn't built for buying decisions.

ideas.title: Fare Cross-Check for Airline Checkout
ideas.oneLiner: An extension that compares the airline's own price with the aggregator price and shows the all-in cost including seat and bag fees, then autofills traveller details.
ideas.problem: Booking directly can cost more than clicking through an aggregator, airline sites are tedious to fill in, and the real price is buried under seat and bag fees.
ideas.targetUsers: Frequent flyers and families booking domestic and international flights, including on Indian carriers.
ideas.monetization: Free core. Premium (about $3/month) for price alerts and saved traveller profiles. Affiliate commission on aggregator click-throughs.
mvp: Detect the airline checkout page and parse the fare
Open a Google Flights/Skyscanner deep link for the same itinerary and compare
All-in cost panel: bags, seat, payment fees
Local-only traveller profile autofill
Alert when the same flight is cheaper elsewhere
Support for 3–4 airlines to start

competitors.name: Google Flights
competitors.gap: Shows the fare, but not the airline's own checkout price or ancillary fees.

competitors.name: Kayak / Skyscanner
competitors.gap: Aggregators with their own markups and upsells; not a check against the direct price.

ideas.title: Domain Transfer and Lockout Guard
ideas.oneLiner: A dashboard that checks that your domains can actually be moved: lock status, auth-code access, registrar account health and expiry, with a transfer-readiness checklist.
ideas.problem: People discover too late that a registrar account was frozen, a transfer was blocked, or a TLD scare made them let a domain lapse. Hosting companies push domain transfers without explaining the exit path.
ideas.targetUsers: Indie developers, small businesses and freelancers who hold a handful of domains with registrars or website builders.
ideas.monetization: Free for 3 domains. ₹149/month for unlimited domains with alerts. One-off 'transfer rescue' checklist PDFs.
mvp: Add domains and read WHOIS/RDAP for registrar, lock status and expiry
Checklist: registrar lock, auth code, admin email still valid
Alert if status flags change, such as hold or pendingTransfer
Email and WhatsApp reminders before expiry
Escape plan page for each registrar: how to get the auth code, who to contact, ICANN complaint form

competitors.name: Registrar dashboards
competitors.gap: Show only their own domains and give no warning before a block.

competitors.name: Uptime/domain monitors
competitors.gap: Alert on expiry, but not on transfer-readiness or registrar lockout risk.

ideas.title: Crowdsourced Rent Price Registry
ideas.oneLiner: A map where renters anonymously post what they actually pay, so anyone can check whether a listing is above the local rate.
ideas.problem: After the RealPage settlement, renters still can't see what neighbours pay while landlords use pricing software. Commenters ask for public rental data to remove the information gap.
ideas.targetUsers: Renters negotiating a new lease or renewal, starting with large cities.
ideas.monetization: Free for renters. Paid data and API for journalists, tenant unions and city planners.
mvp: Anonymous submission: address area, unit size, rent, date, lease length
Proof via a photo of the lease with the personal parts blanked out
Map and per-building median rent
'Is my rent fair?' checker for a listing URL
Rent-change history for each building
Moderation and spam guard

competitors.name: Zillow / Apartments.com
competitors.gap: Show asking rents set by landlords, not what tenants actually pay.

competitors.name: RentCafe
competitors.gap: Averages of listings, with no tenant-reported data.
